<p class="sx-label">Software · 2024 – 2026</p>

# Automated trading system

<p class="sx-lede">Brokers publish trade recommendations every day. I wanted to see what happens if you follow them exactly, without anyone placing the orders by hand.</p>

I built an open-source system that fetches recommendations from ICICI Direct and Paytm Money, using broker APIs and web scraping, and places the orders through the broker's API. Once it is running it needs no manual order entry or daily intervention. A custom screen, the Trade Manager, shows every recommendation and position and lets me add or override trades.

<p class="sx-label">Where the idea came from</p>

## Could a system follow published advice exactly?

Two examples stayed with me: Mohnish Pabrai's account of learning by studying Warren Buffett's decisions, and an investing video by Shankar Nath about systematic imitation. Broker recommendations are only useful if they are acted on quickly and consistently, which is hard to do by hand alongside school. So I narrowed the idea to an experiment: could a transparent system reproduce published recommendations, while still letting me review and step in?
:::

::: {.sx-section}
<p class="sx-label">What I built</p>

## Fetch, check, place, and keep a record

::: {.sx-two}

::: {}
The system collects each new recommendation from the broker: the stock, the price range to buy in, the target and the stop loss. It checks and normalises it, works out the order, and sends it through the broker's API. Every recommendation and its status stays in a table, so I can see what was bought, what is still held, and what was closed at the target or the stop loss.

Fully automatic was not quite enough. Sometimes I wanted to add a trade of my own or correct one the system had made, so I added the Trade Manager: a screen for filtering by source and status, editing prices and quantities, and entering new trades by hand.
:::

<ol class="sx-flow" aria-label="How a recommendation becomes an order">
<li><b>Fetch</b><span>New recommendations from ICICI Direct and Paytm Money</span></li>
<li><b>Check</b><span>Parse the stock, price range, target and stop loss</span></li>
<li><b>Place</b><span>Send the order through the broker's API</span></li>
<li><b>Track</b><span>Record the position until it is closed</span></li>
<li><b>Review</b><span>Override or add trades in the Trade Manager</span></li>
</ol>

:::

::: {.sx-section}
<p class="sx-label">What came next</p>

## From following other people's ideas to testing your own

This system executes someone else's recommendations. It made me want to start one step earlier: how an investor defines an idea in the first place, and checks it against honest market history before trading it. That became [Systematick](/projects/systematick/index-en.html).
:::
